-117.14430,32.72510.name: Naval Medical Center San Diego Infertility Clinic
-117.14430,32.72510.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-1.91400,52.46647.name: P4 London
-1.91400,52.46647.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to Avenues. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-91.86243,36.72770.name: Michelle McDonald
-91.86243,36.72770.desc: Carrier registered with USDA APHIS under the Animal Welfare Act, certificate 43-T-0361. Rats, mice and birds bred for research are excluded from the Act's definition of an animal — the overwhelming majority of animals used, and the great majority of the genetically altered ones. What is covered here is dogs, cats, primates, rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters and farm animals. The rest is counted nowhere.

-106.53939,52.15914.name: Nappan Research Farm
-106.53939,52.15914.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2025
-106.53939,52.15914.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. A site of Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

3.25000,50.51670.name: Groupe Florimond Desprez
3.25000,50.51670.desc: A French family seed company breeding wheat, sugar beet and potato, several centuries old. Family and cooperative ownership still holds a substantial share of European seed, which is why the four-company account of world seed is accurate globally and misleading in Europe.

-121.10000,44.60000.name: Glyphosate-resistant creeping bentgrass — spread into wild Agrostis
-121.10000,44.60000.type: Grass, transgene escape into wild relatives
-121.10000,44.60000.size: Established in wild populations across multiple counties
-121.10000,44.60000.desc: Creeping bentgrass engineered to survive glyphosate, grown in trials for the golf-course market, moved out of its plots into resident populations and hybridised with wild relatives. It is the strongest documented case of transgene spread into wild plant communities anywhere, it was found by accident during unrelated fieldwork, and the plants are still there — eradication was attempted for years and abandoned.

75.71000,19.75000.name: Unapproved herbicide-tolerant cotton planted at scale
75.71000,19.75000.desc: Unapproved herbicide-tolerant cotton was found planted across large areas of India before any approval process had assessed it. The seed moved through informal channels ahead of the regulator, which is a sequence several countries have followed.

103.91920,12.53880.name: Vanny Bio Research
103.91920,12.53880.state: Pursat province, Cambodia — parent company in Hong Kong
103.91920,12.53880.desc: The long-tailed macaque is the most traded primate on Earth, and it is traded because laboratories buy it. Vanny Bio Research runs five breeding facilities in Cambodia and has been the country's largest exporter. In November 2022 US federal prosecutors indicted eight people — two Cambodian Forestry Administration officials and six people connected to the company and its Hong Kong parent — alleging that wild-caught macaques were exported under permits describing them as captive-bred, with as many as 3,000 animals moved that way from at least December 2017. One official was tried in Miami and acquitted in March 2024; the remaining defendants were not arrested, and the allegations against the company have not been tested at trial. What is not in dispute is the trade around it: Cambodian exports ran 13,922 animals in 2019, 29,466 in 2020, 48,160 in 2021, 37,920 in 2022, then fell by roughly two thirds to 13,305 in 2023 as the prosecution proceeded. Satellite imagery shows the Pursat facilities expanding between December 2020 and April 2022. A supply chain that contracts by two thirds when a court starts asking where the animals came from is telling you something regardless of the verdict.

78.57180,17.54490.name: Hylasco Bio-Technology
78.57180,17.54490.desc: Breeds research rats and mice in India under licence from the largest US laboratory animal supplier, using that company's specific-pathogen-free breeding programme, and imports its models and related products. It is accredited by the same international laboratory animal care body that accredits the Chinese and American facilities on this map. The licensing structure is the entry: the genetics are the licensor's, the animals are bred and sold locally, and a researcher in Hyderabad orders from the same catalogue as one in Massachusetts. That is how a standard laboratory organism becomes genuinely global, and it is the same licensing logic the seed facet documents for crop traits.
